This causes a problem because it has to combine all of those to get the amount you are sending then still have enough to be attached to All the NFT’s you have in your wallet already and be able to return the left over. In very specific circumstances it can cause a problem. They are advocating a “be safe” strategy to avoid the potential of an error. Personally, I think that the floor price is negatively influenced by a few things, e.g. wider bear market, several people in here clearly in for the 'gamble' of a legendary or mythic in hope of flipping to make rich quick. 

A lower mint price would be welcomed, as even the 'illusion' of demand by having secondary markets at a small multiple will instill confidence. 

My concerns are about 2 things though:
(1) This is ramping up valuation before launch, which is the opposite of organic growth. There's an increasing risk of asset prices dropping if the numbers of users/gamers don't match expectation in the opening weeks.
(2) There's a large volume of NFT mints planned over the next year. If mint prices are consistently high, I begin to wonder who the audience is, as it sure won't be the average gamer / citizen with just a few hundred bucks in the bank.... If average people get priced out, how do we draw the masses?
